The history of Tarot: from a gambling game to the altar

30 September 2026

Contrary to popular belief, Tarot did not come from Ancient Egypt and was not invented by the Roma. Historians agree: the first decks appeared in northern Italy in the fifteenth century — around the 1440s.

A game for the aristocracy

At first it was a game of the nobility — “tarocchi”. The deck had suits like ordinary cards, and 21 trumps, called “triumphs”. No mysticism at all: the cards were laid out at a table, not on an altar.

The oldest known deck — Visconti-Sforza — had no numbers on the Major Arcana at all. Numbering came later, already to justify a “path” from the Fool to the World.

The eighteenth century: cards become “ancient knowledge”

In the eighteenth century the French occultist Antoine Court de Gébelin decided that ancient wisdom was encoded in the cards. From that moment Tarot turned into a tool of prediction and spiritual practice — in effect, a history it never had was attributed to it after the fact.

1909: the golden age

Arthur Edward Waite and the artist Pamela Colman Smith created the Rider-Waite-Smith deck. Its main innovation: scenes were drawn not only for the Major but for all the Minor Arcana — before that there were just rows of wands and cups. That is why the deck became the gold standard and is still used by most tarot readers.

Where the symbols came from

The symbolism of Rider-Waite gathered several traditions:

  • Christian iconography and alchemy;
  • astrology and kabbalah, added by nineteenth-century occultists;
  • theatre and carnival imagery of the Italian Renaissance;
  • visual archetypes that need no textbook.

About “Death” and “the Hanged Man”

  • “Death” in Tarot is almost never about physical death. It is transformation and the end of a stage — like a snake shedding its skin.
  • “The Hanged Man” in medieval Italy was called “the Traitor” and showed execution for treason. The modern meaning — a pause and a change of angle — appeared much later.

The history of Tarot is a good example of a practice finding meaning later than it is born. Here meaning is made by people, not by cards.
